newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ZHIRINOVSKY SAYS NATO PLANS RECALL HITLER, NAPOLEON.
newsitem.headline: ZHIRINOVSKY SAYS NATO PLANS RECALL HITLER, NAPOLEON.

text.p: Russian ultra-nationalist Vladimir Zhirinovksy said on Saturday that NATO was repeating the mistakes of Napoleon Bonaparte and Adolf Hitler by preparing to expand to the east.

Addressing a crowd of his supporters outside the U.S. embassy in Moscow, Zhirinovsky said NATO's plans to incorporate former communist countries in central and eastern Europe were tantamount to declaring war against Russia.

"The United States, the world's last great power, is about to repeat the mistakes of Napoleon and Hitler," said Zhirinovksy, referring to previous attempts by France and Germany to expand eastwards at Russia's expense.
"(NATO's plans) mean a preparation for war against Russia because NATO is an aggressive bloc," said Zhirinovsky, using the inflamatory rhetoric that has become his trademark.

He threatened to hold demonstrations outside the embassies of other NATO countries in Moscow and said Russia should create a new military bloc that would include Moslem and Asian countries to counter the Western alliance.
Dozens of his supporters waved banners that read "the United States and NATO are destroying Russia" and "NATO's insolence knows no bounds".
Zhirinovsky's bizarrely named Liberal Democratic Party is the second largest in the State Duma (lower house of parliament) after the communists.
There is a rare degree of consensus among nearly all Russia's political factions about NATO's expansion plans, which they see as a direct threat to national security.

Earlier this week President Boris Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, accused NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana of pursuing a covert, anti-Russian policy during a trip to four former Soviet republics
NATO is expected to formally invite several of Moscow's former Warsaw Pact allies to join the alliance at a summit in Madrid later this year. REUTER
